title: Right dg modules and their canonical derived localization
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. An associative unital differential graded $\mathbf Z$-algebra is a monoid object in integer cochain complexes of abelian groups: multiplication is additive in each variable and has $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a d(b)$. A right dg module is a right module object in these complexes, equivalently a module object in the reversed tensor category; its action satisfies $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m d(a)$. Morphisms are degree-zero action-preserving chain maps. Cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms use the underlying complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]; the regular module is $A$ with multiplication. Define $D(A,d)$ to be the Gabriel--Zisman localization at quasi-isomorphisms, equivalently the localization of the dg homotopy category. Its standard triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] has shifts induced by $M[n]^p=M^{p+n}$ with differential $(-1)^n d_M$ and unchanged right action, and distinguished triangles precisely the triangles isomorphic to images of dg mapping-cone triangles. Cones have underlying complex $N\oplus M[1]$, componentwise right action, canonical inclusion, and the signed connecting map in Mathlib\textquotesingle s equivalent cone convention. Include the small coproducts in the component-module universe. Shift comparisons are natural for dg module maps. All comparisons are actual isomorphisms of the specified complexes, not arbitrary replacements of the localization. The tensor product used is [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

mathlib_searches.query: The derived category of right differential graded modules over a differential graded algebra is the localization at quasi isomorphisms
mathlib_searches.verdict: Ordinary derived categories of abelian categories, not dg modules over an arbitrary dg algebra. Reuse the general Gabriel-Zisman localization construction.
Mon and Mod supply the actual dg algebra and module definitions after specialization to cochain complexes and reversed tensor. No dg localization and cone-triangulation interface.
No specialized Mathlib interface. Use Mon, Mod, QuasiIso and MorphismProperty.Localization.
